children: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday ordered the launch of Project Meridian, an initiative aimed at identifying emerging technologies and weapons that could shape future U.S. military capabilities.

The project will examine advances in artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, directed energy, robotics and biotechnology, among other technologies, according to a Sept. 30 memorandum signed by Hegseth and distributed to senior Pentagon leadership, combatant commanders and defense agency officials.

Hegseth directed Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael to commission Project Meridian through a partner organization. The initiative will study potential future battlefields, determine what weapons and technologies U.S. forces may require and recommend ways to develop, test and field those capabilities. The Joint Staff and military services were instructed to connect their future-warfare research efforts with the project.

For investors, the order is notable because it provides another indication of the technology areas the Pentagon may prioritize in future research, procurement and development decisions. Companies involved in AI, autonomous systems, drones and robotics, directed-energy weapons and biotechnology could eventually see opportunities if Meridian's recommendations translate into funded programs. The memorandum itself, however, does not authorize procurement, identify contractors or specify spending levels, making it too early to determine which companies might benefit.

Project Meridian also will draw on expertise outside the Pentagon, including technologists, business leaders, policymakers and national-security specialists. Its mandate is to map how warfare may evolve, identify gaps in U.S. military capabilities and propose solutions consistent with goals in the 2026 National Security Science and Technology Strategy.
“We are witnessing rapid advances in artificial intelligence, autonomy, directed energy, robotics, biotechnology, among other critical high-tech areas,” Hegseth wrote in the memorandum.

The project therefore could serve as an early-stage roadmap for areas that later receive greater Pentagon investment, although its recommendations would still have to move through subsequent budgeting, contracting and acquisition processes before creating material revenue opportunities for defense contractors or technology suppliers.
Hegseth ordered Meridian's final findings and recommendations delivered to his office within 120 days of the announcement, setting a deadline of Jan. 28, 2027.

title: Pentagon launches Project Meridian to identify future warfare technology
